### T-046 — Demote headings embedded in migrated entry bodies

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · open_

A migrated body can still contain a '## ' line (decision.md reports unknown section '## Resolved'),
which the parser reads as a section. The migrator should demote such lines (bold or plain) when it
captures a body, and check should keep reporting them until it does.

### T-152 — Playwright failures have no location in the report

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · open_

A browser-leg failure reaches the aggregate report and the failures bundle with no file and line, so
its Location cell reads — and the failure table cannot point a reader at the spec that failed. The
data is there: the Allure result a Playwright run leaves in allure-results carries a package label
that names the spec (@feasibleone/blong-access.profile.play.ts in the committed history) and a name
label with the test title, so parseResults should read it and set the test entry's file and line.
Two things improve once it does: the report can show where a browser failure is, and provenance can
disambiguate a test name that several specs of one package share, which today falls back to unknown.
The tap leg already has locations, because tap reports them in its own diagnostics, so this is only
the browser leg.

### T-168 — A closed todo id can be re-issued, re-pointing references at another entry

> _2026-09-28 · tools/blong-dev · open_

Closing a todo removes the entry, and nextId in memoryEdit.ts allocates highest existing id plus one
across the workspace memory files, so closing the highest todo frees that number for the next one.
D-299 cited a todo for the trace chunk fix; that number was re-issued to the unrelated login-expire
entry added the same day, so the citation silently resolved to another entry until it was closed and
the audit reported it dangling - and this very entry was handed a recycled number when it was filed.
Frictions and decisions do not have this problem because close keeps their heading under Resolved.
Fix: allocate todo ids from a persisted high-water mark, or keep a closed todo as a Resolved heading
with its id, so an id is never re-issued; the memory pattern page already promises ids are never
reused.

### T-151 — Memory bodies silently flatten bullet lists

> _2026-09-26 · tools/blong-dev · open_

A body handed to `memory add --body-file` (and `memory edit --body-file`) loses its bullet lists:
the items are joined into one paragraph with the `-` markers left inside the text, which then fails
`memory check` with MD031 (a list needs a blank line below it). Measured on D-279 and F-269. Two
ways out, either is fine: teach the writer to keep a list's structure (blank line between blocks,
marker on its own line) so a body may be written as prose or as bullets, or say in the instructions
that a body is prose only, so nobody writes a list and then discovers MD031.

### T-190 — --since cannot filter a Hindsight recall by date

> _2026-10-01 · tools/blong-dev · open_

A search cannot be filtered by date: Hindsight's recall() takes query_timestamp only as a scoring
anchor for relative expressions, and temporal_window ranks rather than filters, so --since was
skipped instead of faked. Three designs were checked against the SDK. Rank recent by passing
temporal_window and then drop the hits older than the boundary client-side, using a new date: tag as
the cheap source of a document's date. Pass only query_timestamp and accept that older material
still surfaces, weighted down. Or pre-filter with listDocuments({timeField: 'updated_at',
startDate}) and keep only those document ids, which is the one native date filter and costs an extra
call. Whichever is chosen, the result header must print the date, and changing the default filter
would invalidate the benchmark in plans/memory-index/eval.

### T-289 — Json and root files are linted by nothing

> _2026-10-10 · tools/blong-dev · open_

Two gaps in what the lint covers. First, `LINT_EXT` and `SPELL_EXT` exclude `.json`, while this
repository eslint config carries a `**/*.json` block, so a package lint checks a `package.json` and
a targeted `blong-dev lint --files package.json` refuses it: the extension table and the eslint
config should agree. Second, the repository root belongs to no Rush project, so `.github/skills/**`
and `cspell.config.yaml` are linted by neither the hook nor `rush ci-lint`; the hook now names them,
and something has to check them — the root can be linted per path with `blong-dev lint --files`, but
the skills carry pre-existing markdownlint debt that a hook checking them would fail on.

### T-313 — blong-dev profile: aggregate a test run's CPU profile per function and line

> _2026-10-10 · tools/blong-dev · open_

A CPU profile answered a question nothing else could — which function a suite's seconds actually
went to — and the throwaway probe that read it has been dropped. `blong-dev profile [glob]` should
run the package's tap suite the way `blong-dev test` does, with `--cpu-prof` added to the child's
`NODE_OPTIONS` and the profiles written to a temp directory, then aggregate the largest profile: sum
`nodes[].hitCount` per `callFrame`, keyed by `functionName @ url:line`, and print the top N as
milliseconds and as a share of the sampled CPU, with the wall time and the sample count as a header.
`--lines` should add a second table built from `nodes[].positionTicks`, one row per line with the
source text beside it — that table is what showed the cost sitting in `LineageIndex.add` rather than
in the sort inside it, and it needs no second run. `--top`, `--json` and `--keep` (leave the
`.cpuprofile` files behind for a viewer such as Speedscope) round it out. Two cautions to carry into
the implementation, both learned on `realm/blong-party`: the line numbers in the profile are the
file's at profile time, so any later source edit silently mislabels them — print the source line and
let the reader notice; and V8 writes the profile when the process exits, so a killed run leaves
nothing to read. The party suite's browser leg is the reference case: 163 s with 75% of its CPU in
`core/semantic-log` before the fix, 8.8 s after.

### T-314 — blong-dev sql should time a statement and show its plan

> _2026-10-10 · tools/blong-dev · open_

The ACL investigation needed one question answered before any other: is the database the bottleneck?
A throwaway probe connected with `mysql2`, ran a statement N times and printed milliseconds per
call, then `EXPLAIN`ed it — and its answer (the whole per-request guard at 0.63 ms, a round trip
at 0.08 ms, an unindexed scan of the largest graph table at 0.07 ms, a plan already using
`access_acl_idx_target` with `Using index`) redirected the work away from indexes, which were never
the cost. `blong-dev sql` should offer that directly instead of leaving the next person to write the
probe: `--time N` runs the statement N times after a warm-up and reports milliseconds per call,
`--explain` prints the plan for the same statement, and both honour the existing connection
resolution (`--config`, `--suite`, `--database`, host and user flags). Reporting the
single-statement case as well as the repeated one matters — the first call pays connection, cache
and warm-up costs — and the pair is how a false lead gets spotted. One guard belongs with it:
`--time` must refuse a statement that is not a read unless the caller asks for it explicitly,
because repeating an `INSERT` is a different experiment from the one that motivated this.

### T-315 — blong-dev log should summarise calls by method, count and duration

> _2026-10-10 · tools/blong-dev · open_

`blong-dev log` prints the most recent entries and stops at 50, and each entry's payload is
pretty-printed across several lines, so counting what a run did meant dumping the whole cache,
stripping newlines and grouping by hand — a shape that made the second sample of a run's work cost
more than the first. What was wanted is the per-method view: the log records `call start: <method>`
and `call end: <method>` with an `id`, a `service` and a `traceId`, so `--summary` should pair them
by id and print, per method, the call count, the total duration and the average, which is the table
that answers where a run's time went. `--method`, `--service`, `--since`/`--until`, `--json`, and a
`--limit` that counts entries rather than lines and is unbounded by default belong with it. The
reference case: the party suite's browser leg makes roughly 450 gateway calls, and naming the
expensive method was guesswork until a hand-written version of this was run against eight thousand
entries; the entries also outlive the process, so this is the only way to ask the question about a
run that has finished — including the tap artifact of a CI run, which carries the same lines.

### T-351 — docs serve --dir should accept an absolute path

> _2026-10-15 · tools/blong-dev · open_

`blong-dev docs serve --dir <path>` joins the path onto the repository root, so an absolute path
silently resolves inside the repo: `--dir /tmp/sb-suite-test` looked for `<repo>/tmp/sb-suite-test`
and reported "has no index.html". Either accept an absolute path as given (the friendlier answer for

> _2026-10-16 · tools/blong-dev · open_

### T-362 — blong-dev ci --run does not accept a run id

> _2026-10-17 · tools/blong-dev · open_

`--run` is a run number, but the number a user copies out of a GitHub URL is the run id
(`/actions/runs/39035957574`), so `blong-dev ci failures --run 39035957574` answers "no run to
diagnose" and the diagnosis needs an extra `gh run view` to learn that the id is #627. Accept
either: when the value matches no recent run number, ask gh for it by id
(`gh run view <id> --json number,headSha,headBranch,status,conclusion,url,displayTitle`) and say in
the answer that an id was resolved rather than a number. The run list already carries `databaseId`,
so the lookup is cheap and the shape is the one `IRunSummary` already uses.

## Done

### T-346 — Name the projects that ran no tests in the CI report

> _2026-10-15 · tools/blong-dev · done_

A project whose `ci-test` fails before it produces a `.ci-report/` is invisible in the CI summary:
the report counts the packages that reported, so a package whose e2e tests never ran reads exactly
like one that has no tests (blong-int-adapter did this for months — @@F-530).

Make it visible. The report tooling (`blong-dev ci-report`) should list the projects that have a
`ci-test` script and produced no report, at least when the tests step failed, and the workflow
should pass that step's outcome (`steps.test.outcome`) to the report step for it. Rush writes each
project's output to `.rush/temp/chunked-rush-logs/<project>.ci-test.chunks.jsonl` in the project
folder, which is enough to tell "the command ran and failed" from "the command never ran" — the
chunk format is one JSON object per line with `kind` and `text`. Failing the job with that list
named is the point: today the only trace of a 180-second wait that timed out is the log of the
project that failed, and the aggregated report says nothing.

Implemented in tools/blong-dev: report/silentProjects.ts with the render section and the
CI_TESTS_OUTCOME gate (the shared workflow passes steps.test.outcome), so a red run names every
package that has a ci-test and no report, distinguishing ran-and-stopped from never-ran.

### T-358 — Render the killing signal in the failure message

> _2026-10-16 · tools/blong-dev · done_

@@F-549 holds the diagnosis: tapReport.ts renders `test process exited with code unknown` and drops

class sits in the same diag block. Render the signal when the exit code is null (and keep the exit

the next red run of that shape: the tool should state the cause class in its first answer, which is
the half of the cost @@F-546 records as not yet dropped.

Done: buildTapRun renders the signal, five unit cases pin the wording, and the live acceptance run
still answers #622. Still unverified end to end: a new published bundle, since the 625 artifact
predates the fix.

### T-361 — Host one shared Allure bundle for every published report

> _2026-10-17 · tools/blong-dev · done_

`BLONG_ALLURE_MAIN_URL` lets every published page load one hosted copy instead of its own bundle,
but nothing publishes that copy yet. The default already takes the storage win: each page gets a
content-addressed `allure-main-<hash>.js` in its publish directory, and the reports repository
deduplicates the identical blobs across packages, runs and alias mirrors. What is missing for the
variable to be useful is a stable location written once per run (a deploy-report input that lands
the file beside the docs tree, or a step that uploads it), plus the workflow setting the variable
before the tests run so the pages reference it. Until then the relative reference is the default and
the variable is the escape hatch; verify it on one tool's report first, because a wrong URL breaks
every report at once.

Implemented as the shared directory mode of externalizeAllureMain: the workflow sets
BLONG_ALLURE_MAIN_URL and BLONG_ALLURE_MAIN_DIR, the bundle is written once and deploy-report copies
it to docs/_assets through its new assets input.
